properties.name: A Decision names the quantities it rests on, each carrying how it was obtained, so the unsourced-quantity report covers decisions too
properties.source: Anthony Sligar (who:ajs), 2026-10-11, choosing option (b) of dec:idea-how-is-a-decision-that-rests-on-numbers-held-to-keeping-its-math: "I like your recommendation of (b) and a smarter (c). let's promote this idea to intent"
properties.statement: A Decision whose answer turns on numbers (a cost, a fit, a size, a yes or no that turns on conditions) records, as structure and not only in its prose, the quantities it rests on. Each has a value with its unit and its provenance, as req:a-quantity-carries-how-it-was-obtained-and-an-unsourced-one-is-reported defines it: measured (by what, when), computed (by which kept computation record, such as a flo2-calc .calc.json registered as an Artifact and linked to the decision with documents), or asserted (by whom). The existing unsourced-quantity report then reads these quantities like any other, so a decision resting on a number nobody sourced is reported, and "asserted by the agent" stays an allowed, visible state, never a refusal. reflow2 still never calls a calculator, and a calculator still never writes into reflow2 (the calculator design's dec:agent-carries-results).
